framework.description: Each criterion is scored 0-10. Multiply by weight. Sum = Composite Score (0-10). Higher is better.

valuation.description: How cheap is the stock on an absolute and relative basis?

score_guide.9-10: Trading at multi-year or historical trough multiples, 40%+ implied upside to DCF/consensus, clear margin of safety
score_guide.7-8: Meaningfully below historical average and peer median, 25-40% implied upside, good margin of safety
score_guide.5-6: Modestly below fair value, 15-25% implied upside, limited but real margin of safety
score_guide.3-4: Near fair value, 5-15% implied upside, minimal margin of safety
score_guide.1-2: At or above fair value, upside depends on multiple expansion that isn't well-supported

key_metrics: Forward P/E vs. sector average and own 5-year average
DCF implied upside using conservative assumptions

balance_sheet.description: Can the company survive and fund itself through the downturn without diluting equity holders?

score_guide.9-10: Net cash position or near-zero net debt, investment grade credit, FCF strongly positive, can self-fund recovery
score_guide.7-8: Low leverage (Net Debt/EBITDA < 1.5x), strong FCF, no near-term debt maturities, investment grade
score_guide.5-6: Moderate leverage (1.5-2.5x), adequate FCF coverage, manageable maturities, investment grade or borderline
score_guide.3-4: Higher leverage (2.5-3.5x), tighter FCF, some debt maturity risk within 2 years, sub-IG possible
score_guide.1-2: Elevated leverage (3.5-4.5x), FCF barely covering interest, maturity wall risk, sub-investment grade
score_guide.0: Distressed balance sheet, refinancing risk, possible covenant breach

catalyst_specificity.description: Are there specific, named, dated, binary catalysts that could drive a re-rating?

score_guide.9-10: 2+ named catalysts with specific dates/events within 12 months, binary outcome (yes/no), any one could drive 15%+ move. Examples: FDA approval date, earnings inflection, contract announcement
score_guide.7-8: 1-2 solid named catalysts within 12-18 months, reasonable probability, meaningful price impact if hit
score_guide.5-6: Catalysts exist but are either slow-moving (multi-year), lower probability, or smaller magnitude. No specific dates/binary outcomes
score_guide.3-4: Vague catalysts without specific triggers, timelines, or names. 'Things might get better' is not a catalyst
score_guide.1-2: No clear near-term catalysts; thesis relies on long-term mean reversion only

positive_patterns.single_event_overreaction: Selloff caused by a single discrete event (trial miss, one-time charge, tariff announcement) rather than slow structural decay. These resolve faster and more completely.
positive_patterns.named_dated_binary: Catalysts that have a specific name (e.g., FARAPULSE), a date (e.g., FDA PDUFA Q4 2026), and a binary outcome (approved/not approved). These create clear re-rating triggers.
positive_patterns.management_action: New CEO, strategic review, cost restructuring — concrete actions management is taking to fix the issue, not just 'hoping things improve'.
positive_patterns.analyst_support_despite_selloff: Strong buy consensus maintained or upgraded during/after selloff. Smart money sees the opportunity.

selloff_quality.description: Is this a high-quality selloff (company-specific, temporary, overreaction) or a low-quality one (structural, justified)?

score_guide.9-10: Classic single-event overreaction — one discrete event caused panic selling, fundamentals intact, market extrapolating worst case. Core franchise undamaged.
score_guide.7-8: Clear company-specific issue that is largely fixable; some uncertainty remains but core franchise undamaged. 1-2 issues, not 5+.
score_guide.5-6: Mix of company-specific and structural issues; fixable but will take time and execution. Multiple compounding factors.
score_guide.3-4: Significant structural headwinds alongside company issues; recovery possible but requires multiple things going right
score_guide.1-2: Primarily structural decline with temporary bounce potential. Chronic underperformance pattern.
score_guide.0: Secular decline — the underlying business is being disrupted and won't recover

competitor_structural_share_loss.condition: Competitor is structurally gaining market share (not just a temporary blip)
competitor_structural_share_loss.examples: LLY gaining GLP-1 share from NVO; SYK gaining ortho share from ZBH

competitive_moat_integrity.description: Is the company's competitive position intact, or is a competitor structurally gaining share?

score_guide.9-10: Monopoly or near-monopoly position intact. No competitor gaining meaningful share. Pricing power preserved.
score_guide.7-8: Strong market position with durable advantages. Minor competitive threats manageable. Share stable or growing.
score_guide.5-6: Solid position but facing credible competitive threats. Share stable but at risk. Moat being tested.
score_guide.3-4: Losing share to a stronger competitor. Moat eroding. Needs investment to defend position.
score_guide.1-2: Structurally losing share. Competitor has superior product/cost/distribution. Moat significantly impaired.
score_guide.0: No moat. Commodity business being disrupted.

macro_alignment.description: Is the current macro environment a tailwind or headwind for this specific stock's recovery thesis?

score_guide.9-10: Macro is a strong tailwind — regulatory support, favorable policy changes, structural demand growth aligns with recovery timing
score_guide.7-8: Macro is neutral to slightly positive — no major headwinds, some tailwinds from policy or cycle positioning
score_guide.5-6: Macro is mixed — some headwinds (rates, regulation) offset by some tailwinds (demand, policy)
score_guide.3-4: Macro is a headwind — regulatory pressure, policy uncertainty, or cycle positioning works against the thesis
score_guide.1-2: Macro is actively hostile — e.g., bipartisan political targeting, active regulatory crackdown, severe cycle risk
score_guide.0: Macro environment makes recovery nearly impossible in the foreseeable future

macro_hostility.condition: Bipartisan political targeting, active regulatory crackdown, or policy environment actively working against the company
macro_hostility.examples: UNH facing bipartisan healthcare reform pressure; tobacco facing global regulatory tightening

analyst_conviction.description: What does the smart money think, and how confident are they?

score_guide.9-10: Strong buy consensus (75%+ buys), low price target dispersion, recent upgrades from credible banks during/after selloff
score_guide.7-8: Majority buy-rated (55-75%), reasonable target dispersion, stable or improving analyst sentiment
score_guide.5-6: Mixed consensus (40-55% buys), moderate dispersion, some recent downgrades offset by holds
score_guide.3-4: Mostly hold-rated (30-40% buys), high target dispersion, recent downgrade cycle
score_guide.1-2: Weak consensus (< 30% buys), sell ratings present, active downgrade cycle ongoing
score_guide.0: Consensus sell, multiple high-profile downgrades, targets coming down sharply

criminal_investigation.trigger: Active DOJ/FBI criminal investigation into company or senior executives
criminal_investigation.action: DISQUALIFIED — automatic fail regardless of score
criminal_investigation.rationale: Criminal investigations create unbounded downside risk: potential fines in billions, executive departures, customer/partner defection, and reputational damage that can take years to repair
examples: UNH DOJ Medicare Advantage fraud investigation
criminal_investigation.override: Only if investigation is formally closed with no charges AND stock hasn't already recovered

chronic_underperformance.trigger: 3+ years of underperforming sector peers with no confirmed inflection point (not just management promises)
chronic_underperformance.action: DISQUALIFIED — automatic fail regardless of score
chronic_underperformance.rationale: Chronic underperformers rarely turn around without a dramatic external catalyst. 'This time is different' is almost never true without concrete evidence of inflection.
chronic_underperformance.confirmed_inflection_required: Must show: (1) specific management action taken (not just announced), (2) early quantitative evidence of improvement (e.g., first quarter of share gains after 12 quarters of losses), (3) external validation (analyst upgrades based on data, not hope)
examples: ZBH chronic share loss to SYK with no confirmed turnaround data

Consumer Staples.notes: Stability premium; volume vs. pricing mix matters

Industrials.notes: Cyclical adjustment needed; use mid-cycle earnings

Utilities.notes: Regulated returns; dividend yield is primary metric

International.notes: Country risk discount; ADR liquidity matters

sector_balance_rule.note: If fewer than 3 sectors have qualifying candidates, document why and proceed with available sectors. Do not force bad picks to meet sector targets.

5.0-6.4.label: SPECULATIVE BUY
5.0-6.4.action: Small position or watchlist; wait for more catalyst clarity

3.0-4.9.label: HOLD / PASS
3.0-4.9.action: Do not initiate; revisit if price declines further

DISQUALIFIED.label: DISQUALIFIED
DISQUALIFIED.action: Hard disqualifier triggered — do not invest regardless of score
